title: Effect of Slurry Aluminizing Parameters on the Microstructure, Phase Composition and Mechanical Properties of Aluminide Coatings on Ferritic Stainless Steel
content: The microstructure and properties of diffusion aluminide coatings are strongly influ-enced by processing conditions, making their optimization essential for controlling coating development. This study investigated the effects of slurry aluminizing temper-ature and treatment time on coatings produced on X3CrTi17 ferritic stainless steel using an inorganic sodium silicate binder. Coatings were manufactured at 700, 800, and 1000 °C for 1, 2, and 6 h and characterized by microscopy, EDS, XRD, and nanoindentation. At 700–800 °C, coatings exhibited distinct compositional boundaries, with Al₅Fe₂ identified as the predominant near-surface phase. At 1000 °C, substantially thicker coatings de-veloped, characterized by an extended diffusion zone, gradual elemental gradients, and AlFe in the near-surface region. EDS analysis also revealed localized Si- and Cr-enriched regions. Empirical regression models described the dependence of coating thickness (R² = 0.981) and mass gain (R² = 0.978) on processing parameters. Nanoindentation revealed coating hardness of approximately 11 GPa, compared with 4–5 GPa for the substrate. The results demonstrate that processing temperature plays a key role in controlling phase formation, diffusion-zone development, and local mechanical properties of slurry alu-minide coatings.
